title: UPDATE: Mississauga boy who died after being shot by Peel Regional Police identified
article: The 15-year-old Mississauga boy who died after being shot by Peel Regional Police has been identified by his family as Ozama Shaw.
The teen died on Saturday, Aug. 26, nearly a month after he was allegedly involved in an armed robbery at a plaza at Creditview and Britannia roads.

The province's Special Investigations Unit, an agency called in to investigate cases of death, serious injury and sexual assault involving police, continues to investigate the circumstances behind the altercation with police.
Around 2 a.m. on July 27, reports say, the boy was one of three individuals involved in an armed robbery at a Petro Canada gas station at the plaza.

The two other suspects, both young men, fled the scene before Peel Regional Police officers arrived, but the teen remained and apparently attempted to rob another establishment and three vehicles in the plaza parking lot.

One witness told reporters how he attempted to break into her vehicle with a gun in his hand. There were also several gunshots exchanged, although its unclear how many were coming from the youth and how many were coming from the police.

Shaw is believed to be among the youngest people killed by police in Ontario. According to The Star, he died at the Hospital for Sick Children after undergoing 11 surgeries and procedures in 30 days to treat a gunshot wound to his abdomen.

"They allowed me to go on the bed with him, so I held him," Kadene, his mother, said in an interview with The Star from her Mississauga home this week. "I still refused to believe, because I didn't want to let go of my baby. It was the hardest thing to do."
Shaw's name and the details of his final days are available only because the family confirmed his identity to the Star.
The family is now attempting to raise money to take Shaw's body back to Jamaica, where his father, grandparents, aunts and childhood friends reside. A GoFundMe page has been set up to fundraise.

"The family is grieving, and needing $12,000 to send him home to the family and to be buried," according to a neighbour who made the page. "Please please please lets help this family and make it just a little tiny bit easier for them by helping to send her son home."
